texts: bad: two things go wrong with the nominalised subject. The parse ranks the LANTERN first on a lighting scale (it says the lantern is the first lantern lit) instead of ranking the lighting, and it turns the noun "lighting" into a lighting-of-the-lantern action rather than treating the lighting itself as the thing being talked about; on top of that, "an occurrence IS a small ritual" has no supported shape at all, so the ritual claim cannot be recorded faithfully however it is parsed. Make the ritual something a Keeper does at that occasion, and keep "the first lighting of a new lantern" as the occasion it happens at: "A Keeper performs a small ritual at the first lighting of a new lantern."

bad: "the vessel of mire-essence" is read as a possession link and, because that link is written possessed-first, it comes out saying the mire-essence owns the vessel; the contents-of-a-container reading has no supported form, so what is actually in the vessel would otherwise have to be dropped. State the containment with a verb so it survives: "Each Council member touches the vessel that holds the mire-essence before the first lighting." (Everything else here is fine — the per-member rule over Council members and the "before the first lighting" ordering both come out right.)

mixed: nothing is lost — the denial correctly covers the whole needing-a-Council-touch claim, and replacement_lantern / council_touch are both broken down into their parts. The shortfall is reach: "A replacement lantern" is a single indefinite thing, so the parse records that one lantern being exempt rather than a standing exemption for replacement lanterns as a class, and it will never apply to any other lantern. Write it as a bare plural to get the general rule: "Replacement lanterns need no Council touch."
